fit.verdict: The best-matched of the four roles, and it keeps getting stronger as the real body of work surfaces. Leroy is a practicing tax preparer who builds the accounting software he uses: ReconcileIQ (an account-reconciliation app with real clients incl. a Form 990 nonprofit), TaxesByRoss (the platform behind his own tax practice), and an extraction-to-books pipeline built on Well (the open-source supplier-invoice extractor by WellApp.ai — he customized it, he didn't write it): a Schedule C category / quarter import bridge, per-client financial dashboards, and a Form 990 auto-fill from the general ledger. That IS Mercury's literal problem statement — getting transactions ready for the books — solved on real client data. Plus TOBA (a live 501(c)(3) platform build with a monthly board-member cadence, full-board product presentations, a written SOP + licensing + continuity-agreement handoff, and three documented board objections he resolved — data sovereignty, duplication, and cost), InsureBridge, and Titan Couriers. All five are built as structured case studies on the Paintbrush /use-cases page — each in its own visual language — plus a standalone 1-page decision record for the TOBA consolidation. TOBA and InsureBridge now carry real product screenshots; ReconcileIQ, Well, and Titan are still on coded mockups aligned to the live marketing previews. The remaining gap is narrow: real screens on the two accounting case studies (ReconcileIQ, Well), and collaboration has been design + stakeholders rather than design + PM + eng + research inside a product org.

criteria.name: 6+ yrs leading complex, end-to-end product design initiatives
criteria.note: 10+ yrs, 'Product Designer & Partner', and a deep bench of shipped products — ReconcileIQ, TaxesByRoss, TOBA (multi-surface, board stakeholders), InsureBridge, Titan, plus the extraction-to-books pipeline customized on Well. No engineering partner or formal research is what keeps it at 8, not 9. (Design leadership itself is now well-evidenced: leads design direction for a 4-person creative team at Paintbrush Marketing across 3,000+ delivered projects.)

criteria.name: Thinks in systems & workflows, not screens
criteria.note: Data-driven architecture, Style Registry governance, the TOBA permissions model, Well's self-healing workflow blueprints and multi-format export system.

criteria.name: Learns new domains obsessively until can challenge experts
criteria.note: He doesn't learn accounting — he has run a private tax practice since 2015 (150+ clients), prepares Form 990 filings on contract for Trydent Consulting (Tallahassee, via Christina Lynch, CEO), built his practice software (TaxesByRoss + ReconcileIQ), and customized the open-source Well extractor into it (Schedule C mapping, quarter routing, 990 auto-fill). Domain operator, not learner.

criteria.name: Turning highly complex workflows into simple experiences
criteria.note: Now backed by real numbers, not just claims. ReconcileIQ: designing for accuracy tools first (guided reconciliation, audit trail, pre-post validation) cut reconciliation time from 2–6 hours to under 90 minutes. TaxesByRoss: per-client quarterly processing went from 1–2 hours to 15–20 minutes. TOBA: a 47-year-old, 500+ member organization that had no system to collect dues at all before this platform. Plus the extraction-to-books pipeline, courier dispatch, checkout, admin intake.

criteria.name: Balances automation with transparency, trust, user control
criteria.note: 'Human-approved, never auto-sends' agents; TOBA audit trail; Well's invoice-data validation, an AI receipt-fraud detector, and 'no passwords stored, GDPR/CCPA'.

criteria.name: Product judgment, clear communication, high ownership
criteria.note: Now well-evidenced across all three sub-signals in the TOBA case study. JUDGMENT: redirected TOBA from 'random information' to systematic feature-by-feature building; scoped the committee consolidation and pitched it to the full board. COMMUNICATION: monthly cadence with the committee-lead board member, full-board product presentations, a written handoff package to the org's marketing lead (SOP intro, Licensing & Continuity Plan, Deploy & Dev SOP, formal Continuity Agreement). ALIGNMENT UNDER DISAGREEMENT: three documented board objections resolved — (1) Finance chair, data sovereignty -> answered in writing: full source-repo access, TOBA-owned domain/DNS, a documented procedure to take over hosting and billing at any time, and a signed path to full ownership, with no proprietary lock-in (free hosting tier, no database/server); (2) Youth Development chair, duplication with an in-progress internal effort -> no forced switch, adoption by comparison once the workspace was real; (3) Leadership Institute chair, infrastructure cost -> none, pro bono, cost scope fixed in the Continuity Agreement (Vercel free + domain, under $25/yr). OWNERSHIP: ships the platform AND wrote the continuity/licensing terms so the org is never stranded. All of this is now packaged — the TOBA case study 'working with the board' section plus a standalone 1-page decision record (decision-record-toba-consolidation.md). Held at 9, not 10: still a volunteer board rather than a product-company PM/eng/research pod, and no formal user research.

criteria.name: Uses AI to accelerate exploration without compromising craft
criteria.note: Provider routing, fine-tuning on past work, explicit 'where AI does not belong' rules, and human-confirm on anything a model touches. The extraction-to-books pipeline is the applied case: an AI extractor (open-source Well) feeds structured data, and every row is categorized, quarter-assigned, and reviewed by a person before it lands in the books. AI as a tool, never a replacement — matches the résumé's stated stance.
